title: a-grace fixture has a split identity: client shows 'Grace Kelly', baked PDF says 'Gráinne Foley' — the r1 real-person-name fix never landed on the client fixture
evidence: demo_fixtures.gleam:93: "first_name":"Grace","last_name":"Kelly","email":"grainne.foley@example.ie" — pdf_prebake.gleam:424: applicant_name: "Gráinne Foley", (and pdf_prebake row_grace base_row args "Gráinne", "Foley", "grainne.foley@example.ie") — demo_store.gleam:1435: #("a-grace", "RightTenantry-Report-Grace-Kelly.pdf"), — r1-consolidated.json warning: "Fixture uses a real person's name ('Grace Kelly') attached to a rejected/eviction/CCJ story | client/src/demo/demo_fixtures.gleam:93"; r2 briefing fold list claims "the real-person fixture swapped (Gráinne Foley…)"
detail: The r1 warning-fold swapped the email and the PDF-side name to Gráinne Foley but left the client fixture's first/last name as 'Grace Kelly' (a famous real person) on the eviction/CCJ story. Downloading that applicant's report yields a PDF titled 'Gráinne Foley' while the UI and download filename say 'Grace Kelly' — three surfaces disagree about one entity, and the real-person exposure ships.
recommended_fix: Rename the client fixture (demo_fixtures.gleam:93 and demo_store.gleam:1435 filename) to Gráinne Foley so the UI, the baked PDF, and the download filename carry one synthetic identity.

title: lint_demo_network.py's 35-line guard window ignores message-arm boundaries — an unguarded real api call passes the lint when any unrelated demo_mode mention sits within 35 lines above it
evidence: lines 144-145 walk back only to NAME the enclosing arm: `for j in range(idx - 1, -1, -1):` / `if re.match(r"^    (User|App|Api|Browser|msg\.)[A-Za-z0-9_]+", lines[j]):` — lines 162-163 then check the guard with no scope respect: `window = "\n".join(lines[max(0, idx - 35) : idx])` / `guarded = "model.demo_mode" in window or "updated_model.demo_mode" in window`. Probe on this tree: injecting an unguarded `notification_api.fetch_notifications` into a fresh arm 3 lines below an arm containing `case model.demo_mode` exits 0 ("demo no-network lint clean"); the identical call without the nearby mention exits 1.
detail: The Pillar-1 structural guard's window spans arm boundaries, so a future real api call in a new arm placed below any demo-branched arm silently passes CI. All currently passing calls were verified same-arm-guarded, so the bypass is latent, not live.
recommended_fix: Cut the window at the enclosing arm/function boundary found in the existing backward walk (stop the slice at lines[j] of the arm match), so 'model.demo_mode' must appear within the same scope as the call.

title: CI demo-no-network grep has blind spots: real api-module imports anywhere in demo/ and arbitrary fetch usage inside demo_api.gleam both pass
evidence: VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rn "api_helpers" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true) / RSVP_VERBS=$(grep -rnE "rsvp\\.(send|get|post|put|patch|delete)" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" || true) / FETCH_VIOLATIONS=$(grep -rln "gleam/fetch" client/src/demo/ --include="*.gleam" | grep -v "demo_api.gleam" || true) — lint_demo_network.py scans only client.gleam (`path = "client/src/client.gleam"`); verified no demo/*.gleam currently imports client/api/* so no live violation.
detail: A demo/ module importing client/api/notification_api (no 'api_helpers' string) passes the grep, and lint_demo_network.py never scans demo/; demo_api.gleam is exempted wholesale, so a non-static-PDF fetch there passes too. Latent guard hole, no current offender.
recommended_fix: Extend the grep to ban `client/api/` imports (or the eight api module names) across client/src/demo/, and pin demo_api.gleam's single fetch to the /static/demo/report- prefix (e.g. grep the URL constant).

title: pdf_prebake reports 'FAILED: n of m PDFs failed' but always exits 0, and swallows the output-directory creation error
evidence: case simplifile.create_directory_all(out_dir) { Ok(_) -> Nil Error(_) -> Nil } … case failures { 0 -> io.println("Pre-baked " <> …) _ -> io.println("FAILED: " <> int_to_string(failures) <> " of " <> int_to_string(list.length(results)) <> " PDFs failed") } — no halt/nonzero exit anywhere in main()
detail: A regen run with typst missing or an unwritable directory prints failures to stdout but exits 0 — a scripted/CI regen step cannot detect it, so stale or absent PDFs ship silently behind a green step.
recommended_fix: Halt with a nonzero exit code (erlang halt) when failures > 0, and surface the create_directory_all error instead of discarding it.

title: demo_analytics_ffi.mjs invokes posthog.has_opted_in_capturing() outside the try/catch — a throwing consent check escapes the documented fail-open posture
evidence: function can_capture() { return ( … typeof window.posthog.has_opted_in_capturing === "function" && window.posthog.has_opted_in_capturing() && … ); } — export function capture(event, props_json) { if (!can_capture()) return undefined; try { const props = …; window.posthog.capture(event, props); } catch (_) {} — header claims "a missing posthog, a throw, or a revoked consent all no-op"; the pre-approved model bridge (meta_pixel_ffi.mjs) guards with typeof checks only, which cannot throw
detail: Unlike meta_pixel's guard, this one calls a third-party method before the try. If has_opted_in_capturing throws (e.g. persistence/localStorage unavailable), the exception propagates into Lustre's init/update (enter_demo fires capture_event at boot), potentially blanking /demo.
recommended_fix: Wrap the can_capture() invocation (or just the has_opted_in_capturing() call) in try/catch inside capture(), matching the file's own documented fail-open contract.
